question: Rockets work on the principle of conservation of ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Momentum.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rockets work **on the principle of **conservation of Momentum**, which is derived from Newton's third law of motion.
 
• **The rocket expels mass (propellant) at high speed, and in turn, the rocket moves in the opposite direction.**
 
• In a rocket, gasses at high temperatures and pressure are created by the combustion of fuel.
 
• They escape with a high constant velocity via a nozzle.
 
• The large, backward momentum of the gasses gives the rocket an equal forward momentum.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Conservation of Momentum: According to this principle, in an isolated system, the vector sum of linear momenta of all bodies of a system is conserved and is not affected due to their mutual action and reaction.
 
• If two bodies of different masses collide with each other and there is no external force acting on it them,
 
• The initial momentum of bodies = Final momentum of bodies
